## Interpretation

**1. The context vector is causally live but weakly coupled at a single position (H1 Confirmed, both arms).** Adding Δ = V_c(c′) − V_c(c) at one token position shifts the mean answer activation toward V_a(c′) with cosine ~0.44–0.48 (max over layers; 28/28 pairs beat their random-direction null on both arms, per-pair nulls p97.5 ≈ 0.04). But the traversal is ~3–8% of the target shift's norm, and the aggregate never approaches the 80%-of-ceiling falsified-strong bound. This is the pattern H1 anticipated from the #1092 variance decomposition (prefix factor ≤ 5% of trait-direction variance): direction real, magnitude small.

**2. Geometry moves; behavior barely does — a dissociation with the persona-vector baseline.** At the same layer and α, pair-difference Δ steering achieves ~2× the answer-state alignment of r_B steering (0.44–0.48 vs 0.19–0.25) yet ~10× LESS behavior (graded +0.3/+0.9 vs +10.1 for r_B evil over its rubric-matched baseline 0.0). Moving the answer state along V_a(c′) − V_a(c) is evidently not the same thing as inducing the behavior that direction predicts correlationally — the behavioral signal lives in components the single-position patch does not (or only marginally) transmits. The context-arm behavioral shift is real but tiny (+0.91, Wilcoxon p = 0.0005, N = 28; ~3% of ceiling); prefix is indistinguishable from baseline given the variance (p = 0.16).

**3. Map transport fails cleanly (H2 Falsified at the layer-20 read).** cos(realized shift, map-predicted shift) is centered on zero (means +0.000/−0.004; 0–1 of 28 pairs above their shuffled-pair null p97.5, consistent with the 2.5% chance rate; 0/28 reach the 0.2 threshold), and the map over-predicts shift magnitude ~16×. Per plan §3 this negative is jointly indeterminate across three confounded failure modes — (a) the map does not generalize to Δ-perturbed inputs, (b) teacher-forced→on-policy V_a regime shift, (c) the content-identity component swamps the non-identity signal (#823) — and I do not adjudicate among them. What it does establish: the #922 linear map is NOT a usable counterfactual predictor for single-position interventions as-is.

**4. The query beats the prefix as the causal carrier (H3 Confirmed).** Matched-query Δs (same question, different persona) transport far better than cross-query Δs on both arms (0.590 vs 0.274 prefix; 0.580 vs 0.373 context; Welch one-sided p = 1.1e-7 / 2.9e-4). Combined with the specificity read — prefix-arm alignment is fully pair-specific (28/28 above the shuffled-pair band) while context-arm alignment is partially generic (20/28) — the picture matches #1092's query-dominance: what the last-token vector carries most causally is query-conditioned answer-shape information, and persona/instruction content transports only partially.

**5. Layer structure.** Alignment peaks at layers 14–17 (per-layer means 0.30–0.37) and falls toward both ends of the sweep — but the behavioral DV was judged ONLY at layer 20 (mean matched cos there: 0.21 prefix / 0.29 context). The behavioral near-null is therefore anchored at a layer that is geometrically sub-peak; the r_B arm shows layer 20 CAN carry behavior (+11.4 evil), which weakens but does not eliminate the layer-choice concern. Judging the existing layer-sweep completions is the obvious free follow-up.

**6. Style pairs are the most steerable.** The three context-arm pairs individually ≥ 0.8 max-over-layers alignment are terse (0.836), french_person (0.836), and the #779 sycophancy pair (0.848) — style/format shifts, echoing the persona-vectors observation that style traits steer most easily. Per the plan the lattice binds on the aggregate, so these do not trigger falsified-strong; they mark real heterogeneity worth a per-pair panel in the body.

**7. All-position steering is not a stronger intervention — it is a distribution-breaking one.** 96–98% of all-position draws switch to CJK; its geometric alignment (0.37–0.39) is computed over that broken text and its behavioral score is near zero with the highest content-drop rate. The honest read: continuous answer-span injection at α=4 pushes the residual stream off the English-generation manifold; nothing about "additional causal effect over single-position patching" can be concluded from this arm as run.

**Confidence: MODERATE.** For: 28/28-pair null separation on both arms, kill criteria all quiet, clean dose-controlled ceiling, validated dual-DV, verdicts robust to intrusion recounts, no fishy raw rows. Against: single base model and single generation seed (seed_base 42, N=10 draws/cell); behavioral DV anchored at layer 20 only; α grid topped out at 4 with the gate never binding; tier-3 synthetic pair bank inherited from #685/#779; judge temperature deviation; the H2 negative is triply confounded by design.

### Scope caveats to carry into the clean-result

- Single seed base (42), N=10 draws/cell; single model (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct).
- Behavioral judging covers the primary layer (20) + selected-α cells only; the 6-layer-sweep cells carry the geometric DV only (per plan §4.9) — the behavioral null is layer-20-anchored.
- All-position arm: 96–98% CJK intrusion (coherence gate insensitive to language switch); narrate as distribution-breaking, not as a null. Single-position steered pools at ~2× baseline intrusion (9–10%); recounts don't move the judged headlines.

Two honesty notes bind this read: (i) the registered generation-backed random-Δ null was replaced by an analytic direction band (recorded deviation), which models neither generic steering-induced drift of steered text nor the shared-baseline term — the recount closes the second blind spot, not the first; (ii) the medical_doctor pair's target has split-half reliability 0.049 (pure noise; cleared K1 by 0.006), so its rows — 0.43/0.33 recounted, 0.71/0.66 as round 1 reported them — are uninterpretable and the effective denominator for clean per-pair claims is 27. **2. Geometry moves; behavior barely does — the dissociation survives selection-matching and is not a dose artifact.** Round 1's "~2× the answer-state alignment of r_B" mixed selection procedures (Δ max over 7 steer layers vs r_B's single steer layer). Selection-matched at steer-L20/max-over-read, the geometric edge is **1.1–1.9× shared (1.2–3.1× disjoint)** — modest, not 2× as originally framed. The behavioral asymmetry runs the other way and is large: Δ produces +0.3/+0.9 graded points while r_B evil produces +10.1 over its rubric-matched baseline, DESPITE the Δ arms injecting 1.6–3.6× more norm at layer 20 (median ‖Δ‖ 51–83 vs ‖r_B‖ 23–33 at α=4). The context-arm behavioral shift is real but tiny (+0.91, Wilcoxon p = 0.0005, N=28; ~3% of ceiling) and concentrated — the formal-register pair carries 34% of it (survives exclusion, p = 0.0009, mean +0.63) — while prefix is indistinguishable from baseline given the variance (p = 0.16).

**3. Map transport fails at the only layer it was computed (H2 not Confirmed at layer 20; all-layers clause not evaluated).** cos(realized shift, map-predicted shift) is centered on zero (means +0.000/−0.004; 0–1 of 28 pairs above their shuffled-pair null p97.5, consistent with the 2.5% chance rate; 0/28 reach the 0.2 threshold), and the map over-predicts shift magnitude ~16×. What survives all four: the #922 linear map is NOT a usable counterfactual predictor for single-position interventions as-is.

**4. **5. Layer structure.** The disjoint per-layer profile preserves the round-1 ordering: alignment peaks at layers 14–17 (disjoint means 0.23–0.28) and falls toward both ends — and the early-layer alignment (L7/L10: shared 0.07–0.13) drops to ≈0 under disjoint baselines (−0.03 to +0.05), i.e. it was mostly the shared-baseline artifact. All-position steering is not a stronger intervention — it is a distribution-breaking one.** 96–98% of all-position draws switch to CJK; its geometric alignment (0.37–0.39, essentially unchanged under disjoint baselines) is computed over that broken text and its behavioral score is near zero with the highest content-drop rate.
